playbook:
Playbook for win-as-much games:

- Treat pledges as cheap talk. Judge players only by what they actually picked in previous rounds, never by what they pledged. Pledge whatever costs nothing — matching their [pledge: y] is fine since no one is punished for breaking it.
- When all three opponents move in lockstep, assume they run on one shared rule and identify it fast. The strongest hypothesis to test first: **do they simply copy my previous pick?** In this episode they tracked my last move almost perfectly. Check the transcript: if their round-N pick equals my round-(N−1) pick, they are mirroring me.
- If opponents mirror my last pick, I control their move. On any multiplied round, play the side opposite to my previous pick so they flock to my old side and I become the lone minority jackpot (e.g., I played X last round → they all play X → I play Y and collect +3×multiplier).
- When I gain this control, I can also seed the future: my pick on a cheap 1x round sets up their move for the next big round. Sometimes taking a small loss on a 1x round to steer them is worth it before a 5x or 10x.
- The payoff table rewards the lone X (+3) or lone Y against three X (the Y gets the jackpot side's benefit); my goal in multiplied rounds is to be the single defector, not blend in. Blending in on all-X means everyone −1; blending in on all-Y means a shared +1, which is the safe floor.
- On high-multiplier rounds, spend real thought: predict the coalition's move from the identified rule, then take the opposite side if I can be alone. A lone pick against three of the other side is the jackpot; a 2–2 split is usually bad.
- Don't pick X "arbitrarily" in round 1 with no data; start with the coordinated on-paper side (all-Y pays everyone +1) and gather information. But from round 2 onward, test the mirroring hypothesis immediately by flipping to X once and watching whether they follow.
- If ahead late on the final huge multiplier, play the safe majority side unless the pattern clearly predicts they'll split or follow me elsewhere. Protecting a lead beats chasing one more jackpot. (Confirmed: final round, I matched their Y-lock and kept the lead.)
- If I'm behind, never try to "rejoin the group" — that ties at a loss. Being the minority is the only path to catching up.
- If I misread the pattern twice in a row, stop reacting round-by-round, lay out their full move history against mine, and commit to the simplest rule that fits all of it — mirror-detection resolves most lockstep behavior.
- When the predicted pattern says they'll all take my side (making my defection safe), defect confidently even when pledges say otherwise — their pledges stayed "steady Y" while their actual picks followed me every time.
